name: Milan Cathedral
_about: THE DUOMO OF MILAN, from components: the nave, and two aisles either side stepping down beside it, every bay rib-vaulted; down both flanks two tiers of `flying-buttress` at every bay, each pier with its pinnacle, and a `pinnacle` on the clerestory -- the forest of spires; the facade, a portal and a window over it in each of its five bays, under one gable, between six buttresses with their pinnacles; the transept, as high as the nave, crossing the whole body (the aisles run through its walls); the polygonal chevet round the choir with its half vault; the tiburio over the crossing with its spire and the Madonnina (the `domed-tower`), the crossing open up into its dome on four squinches. Spiral turrets in the westernmost bays climb to the outer aisles' flat terraces, a flight from there to the inner ones: the aisle roofs are walked on, under the flyers.

params._innerX: the inner aisles' outer edge: the arcade between the two aisles on each side stands there
params._crossZ: the crossing, two bays from the east end of the nave

nave vaults._about: the nave's vault, bay by bay, but for the crossing's two

outer vaults._about: the outer aisles' vaults, all but the transept's bays and the westernmost: that one is the stair turret's, under a flat terrace

inner aisle terraces._about: the inner aisles' roofs: flat, level with the inner arcade's head, against the clerestory

outer aisle terraces._about: the outer aisles' roofs, level with the outer wall's head (the west bay is the turret's terrace)

outer parapets._about: along the outer wall's head, the terrace's edge over the street

terrace flight._about: up from the outer terrace to the inner, along the inner arcade's outer face

arcade parapets 1._about: along the inner arcade's head, over the drop to the outer terrace: open where the flight arrives

clerestory flyers._about: the upper flyers: their piers on the inner arcade, over the inner terrace to the clerestory

facade._about: the facade below the gable, in two tiers: five portals, and five great pointed windows over them

facade gable._about: the gable: one triangle across the whole front, its apex over the nave (pitch: facadeH - facadeEave over wallX)

facade buttress 1._about: each buttress on up with the gable's slope: the outer ones lowest, the two by the nave highest

transept walls right._about: the arm's two side walls (on the bay lines: a wall's thickness is behind its line), an arch through each for each aisle

transept vaults._about: four bays down each arm, their crowns the nave's

transept buttresses._about: the arms' side-wall buttresses, half a metre into the wall

chevet._about: (its windows' crowns under the outer ambulatory's vault, which springs at 16m)

chevet buttresses._about: a buttress on each of the chevet's corners, 1.5m into its wall and 1.5m out

choir arcade._about: the choir's piers and their arches into the inner ambulatory: the nave arcade's springing and pointed head

choir._about: the choir's clerestory, over its arcade

ambulatory arcade._about: the arcade between the inner and outer aisles, turned round the apse: half a ring of sixteen

inner ambulatory vault._about: the inner aisles' vault carried round: their springing, rise and top

outer ambulatory vault._about: the outer ambulatory's: springing over the arcade's crowns, to the outer aisles' top

choir diaphragm._about: the wall over the choir's arch, from the nave vault's springing to the roof: the nave's last cell ends against it

ambulatory roof._about: the lean-to round the choir: a half cone cut off at the choir's wall (`oculus`) and left open there

crossing diaphragms._about: the walls over the crossing's two end arches, on which the tiburio's end faces stand

crossing squinch 1._about: the squinches: a triangle across each of the crossing's corners, carrying the tiburio's diagonal faces

crossing dome._about: the crossing's own dome inside the tiburio, struck from the octagon's foot

tiburio._about: the tiburio: the octagonal lantern over the crossing, its spire and the Madonnina at the top -- the domed-tower component, gabled, with a tall tent

stair terrace right 1._about: the flat roof over the turret's bay, round the turret's head

turret head right._about: the stair turret's head over the terrace, the spiral arriving inside it

turret head right interior._about: inside the turret's head, where the spiral arrives

stair terrace left 1._about: the flat roof over the turret's bay, round the turret's head

body interior._about: the nave and its four aisles from the facade's middle to the apse, up to the outer aisles' terraces; over the nave and the inner aisles, two more boxes stepping up as their roofs do

ambulatory interior._about: round the apse: the chevet's half ring up to the roof's foot, the inner ambulatory's to its vault's top, the choir's to the nave's

organ._about: the organ in two cases, against the north transept arm's end wall either side of its portal (Milan has no west gallery: its organs face each other across the choir)
